item.title: Group Dynamics
item.description: Current Projects: Judgement & decision-making Information sharing Judgment & decision-making Group decisions are ubiquitous in everyday life. Even when decisions are made individually, decision-makers often receive advice or suggestions from others. Thus, decisions are often social in nature and involve multiple group members. The ways group members combine their preferences to make a group decision generally falls along two dimensions: how much interaction or information exchange is allowed among the group members and how the final decision is made.

item.title: Moral/Political
item.description: Current Projects: Moral foundations Political extremism Moral foundations The trolley problem has been used in moral psychology for its ability to capture both cognitive and emotional approaches to moral judgment. In the switch dilemma, a runaway trolley is headed for five workers who will be killed if it proceeds on its present course (Thomson, 1985). To save them, one must throw a switch, turning the trolley so it will kill one person instead of five.
